main_table4.author_prose: Authors explicitly state no association with levels of fasting glucose in any of the three cohorts. DESIR printed additive P=0.05 is boundary/rounded and visually bold; retain this alongside their prose rather than silently treating the whole table as strictly null.

supp_table8.population: European non-diabetic population-based subjects; main prose describes these as untreated nondiabetic individuals
supp_table8.positive_fpg_detail: DESIR recessive P=0.02 is a published nominal FPG association, with TT lower than CC/CT. Other supplement FPG models are nonsignificant at 0.05. Do not replace this with a blanket claim that Rung never tested/reported FPG.

published_fpg_results.models: Both tables use linear regression adjusted for gender, age and BMI; additive, dominant and recessive models; DESIR mixed models account for four follow-up times. Current HUFS uses an additive model of log-FPG with age/sex/BMI/one EIGENSTRAT axis. No cross-study effect/outcome judgment made.
published_fpg_results.separate_phenotypes: Rung Table3 hyperglycemia combines T2D and impaired fasting glucose and is not the same endpoint as continuous FPG. Table8 OGTT AUC glucose has nominal associations (Padd0.042/Pdom0.03), also distinct from fasting plasma glucose.

conditional_evidence_answers.question: Was FPG actually tested and published in Rung2009?
conditional_evidence_answers.answer: Yes: main Table4 and supplement Table8 publish rs2943641–FPG tests, including nulls and a DESIR recessive nominal positive. The title/abstract alone would miss this.

conditional_evidence_answers.question: Does evidence establish a general positive additive rs2943641–FPG finding across cohorts?
conditional_evidence_answers.answer: No such positive across-cohort statement was found. Main prose says no FPG association; main DESIR additive P is printed0.05; supplement DESIR additive0.06, recessive0.02. Preserve model and population distinctions.

conditional_evidence_answers.question: What does current report empirically test at IRS1?
conditional_evidence_answers.answer: Continuous FPG in927 unrelated non-diabetic African-Americans, using local LD proxies (r2≥0.3); rs2943641 itself unavailable for direct testing. Table2 lists10 proxy results and places reported SNP p-value5×10−2 beside rs2943641. This matches printed main DESIR additive P0.05 numerically, but the current text does not explicitly map that value to DESIR/Table4, so provenance of that p-value remains conditional.

conditional_evidence_answers.question: Is the Rung link only an untested new phenotype near a diabetes locus?
conditional_evidence_answers.answer: Original FPG was empirically tested and published, so that specific premise is false. Whether current proxy/additive analysis re-tests a particular original null, boundary or recessive finding versus extends the locus requires parent scientific adjudication of the exact claim/model/allele and LD correspondence; locus overlap and the current authors replication label alone do not settle it.

conditional_evidence_answers.question: Do closest-chain findings duplicate shipped Dupuis2010?
conditional_evidence_answers.answer: Current table/catalogue separates Rung rs2943641 from the16 MAGIC FPG SNPs assigned to shipped Dupuis2010. However the review assertion that Dupuis has no IRS1 evidence at all would be too broad: its main text reports rs4675095 HOMA-IR P4.6×10−3, says that SNP is not in LD with rs2943641, and reports rs2943641 C associations with FI P0.02/HOMA-IR P0.04 in discovery. These are insulin/resistance traits, not an identified later FPG retest in the inspected main text. No evidence here establishes that HUFS rs2943641-proxy FPG is duplicating a Dupuis FPG result; no exhaustive negative conclusion about uninspected Dupuis supplements is warranted. Parent retains closest-chain/identity decision.

current_population.quote: The individuals studied were unrelated nondiabetic participants over the age of 20 years (n=927) enrolled in the HUFS. This population-based study of African-Americans in the Washington, DC metropolitan area has been previously described by Adeyemo et al. [6]. For the present study, participants with FPG ≥7 mmol/l or who were receiving treatment for diabetes were excluded.

current_selection.quote: Replication analysis was performed on SNPs identified in GWASs of FPG based on information in the National Human Genome Research Institute's catalogue of published GWASs (www.genome.gov/gwastudies/). The query returned hits indicating reported SNPs, their respective p values and associated genes (ESM Table 2). If multiple studies reported the same SNP, the SNPs with the lowest p value were included in the present study. The returned results included 16 SNPs associated with FPG in the Meta-Analyses of Glucose and Insulin-related traits Consortium (MAGIC) study [2]. The MAGIC SNPs were supplemented by 13 additional SNPs from previously published GWASs (ESM Table 2) for a total of 29 SNPs that we attempted to replicate in our African-American cohort.

current_unavailable.quote: We note that SNPs in C2CD4B, FADS1, GCK and G6PC2 from the MAGIC study and IRS1, PDE4B, and ATP8B4 from other GWASs were not directly compared in the HUFS dataset owing to quality-control filters or lack of genotyping or imputation data.

current_ld_result.quote: We also analysed SNPs that were in LD (r 2 ≥0.3) with each discovery SNP (ESM Fig. 1). This replication strategy, which queried a 500 kb window centred on the index SNP, yielded a total of 317 SNPs located in or near nine different genes or unknown gene region (G6PC2, GCKR, MTNR1B, DGKB-TMEM195, TCF7L2, SLC30A8, AK024684, ZMAT4 and IRS1). Thirty-eight SNPs distributed across all nine gene regions of the 317 SNPs tested were significantly associated with FPG after Bonferroni correction for multiple comparisons (Table 2).

dupuis_irs.quote: Although not reaching genome-wide-significance, we note that SNP rs4675095 in the insulin receptor substrate-1 gene (IRS1) was also associated with HOMA-IR (P=4.6×10−3), which given IRS1’s excellent biological credentials will warrant further investigation. This SNP is not in LD with the widely studied missense SNP G972R (rs1801278) nor with the newly discovered T2D SNP rs294364145, whose C risk allele was only nominally associated with increased FI (P=0.02) and HOMA-IR (P=0.04) in our discovery dataset.

verification.offset_convention: Zero-based Unicode character and UTF-8 byte offsets, end exclusive, in exact named saved text file. Quotes generated by direct contiguous slicing; no dehyphenation, whitespace normalization, OCR repair or column splicing.
